My doctoral work asks how social contact, mobility and attitude data can be used
to understand and forecast the behavioural drivers of epidemic dynamics. It
builds on a background in mathematics and health data science, and on earlier
work using branching process models to estimate the probability that an
introduction becomes a major epidemic.

I also work in health economics, on cost-utility modelling and economic
evaluation of blood-borne virus screening interventions: coding
hepatitis B progression models, evaluating TB IGRA testing in high-risk groups,
and micro-costing digitally enhanced BBV testing.
